turns.doctor_question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, because it's probably just normal stress or something, but... well, what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting these little things that I normally handle without any problem. 

It's actually a bit embarrassing to admit, especially since I work as a secretary and I'm supposed to be the organized one, you know? But lately I keep dropping the ball on silly things, like forgetting to return phone calls, or not turning in a simple registration form, or just forgetting to stop for an errand on the way home. It's nothing huge, but it's just not like me. I just wanted to make sure I'm okay... is that an alright reason to come in?

symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly states they keep forgetting daily tasks such as returning phone calls, turning in forms, and running errands.

turns.doctor_question: When these memory lapses occur, would you say your mind feels distracted or cluttered with other thoughts, or does it feel more like your mood is low and you just lack the energy or motivation to keep track of things?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um, definitely not low mood or a lack of energy. I actually really like my job and I'm usually a very upbeat person! I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm depressed or anything. 

It's... I guess it's more the distracted thing? I don't want to sound like I'm not paying attention at work, because I really do try my best, but... well, at the office, it seems like if just one phone rings, or if I hear people talking nearby, I just kind of lose my place. Or even just a random thought about something I need to do at home will pop into my head and completely pull me off what I was working on. 

I mean, everyone gets sidetracked by office noise sometimes, right? I'm sure it's pretty normal to get a little cluttered like that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily pulled off task by extraneous stimuli like a ringing phone, nearby conversations, or unrelated thoughts.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies having a low mood or being depressed, stating they are usually very upbeat.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient denies a lack of motivation or interest, noting that they actually really like their job.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient explicitly denies experiencing a lack of energy.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your life, did you experience these same kinds of difficulties with staying focused or being organized when you were a child or in school?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, if I'm being completely honest... I guess I did have some of those moments back then, too. I was a good kid, I promise! I never wanted to be difficult or anything. But, um... yeah, even back in elementary school, I was sort of the kid who would forget to hand in permission slips, or I'd do my homework and then somehow completely lose it in the bottom of my backpack. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to look back on. My mom and my teachers usually had to... well, they kind of had to remind me step by step to make sure I actually finished my projects. I always just thought I was a bit of a daydreamer, and I really did try my best to keep up. I mean, a lot of kids are a little scatterbrained when they're little, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it was... does that answer your question okay?

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports needing step-by-step reminders from teachers and their mother to ensure they actually finished their school projects.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly mentions losing their completed homework in the bottom of their backpack.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient describes being forgetful in daily school routines, such as forgetting to hand in permission slips.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from these issues with focus and organization, do you often find yourself feeling restless, or do you find that you have a hard time sitting still for long periods of time?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um, restless? No, I wouldn't say I'm restless. I'm definitely not one of those people who has to be running around all the time, I promise! I can sit at my desk just fine. 

But, well... I guess if I'm in a really long meeting, or back when I was in longer classes, I might do little things. Like, I'll catch myself clicking my pen, or maybe my foot will start bouncing a bit. Sometimes I kind of shift around in my chair, even when I'm really trying my hardest to just sit perfectly still and pay attention to whoever is talking. 

It's just nervous energy, I think! I never get up and disrupt anything or bother anyone. I try to keep it really quiet so nobody notices. I mean, everyone gets a little fidgety when they have to sit for a really long time, don't they? I hope that doesn't make me sound hyper or anything... is that normal?

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes clicking their pen, bouncing their foot, and shifting around in their chair during long meetings or classes.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they can sit at their desk just fine and never get up to disrupt anything.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly denies feeling restless or being someone who has to run around all the time.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient denies being someone who has to be running around all the time.
